spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: The Purification of the Mind by Descent and Removal

---

**¶1:** When Divine Providence expelled these three containing forms from the interior mind — those of falsity, of spiritual darkness, and of evil love — did it perhaps cast them directly into the outermost states of confinement at the boundary of the rational mind? Or did it first bring them down into the natural mind, and then sweep them from the natural mind and cast them into their appointed places of confinement?

**¶2:** When Divine Providence was about to expel these three containing forms, it poured all three into the natural mind, one by one at the appointed order and season. It expelled them and brought them down into the external man.

**¶3:** Then it drew them out and separated them from the natural mind by means of three coverings of external truth — those of spiritual influx, of genuine truth, and of purified love — which clothe the Divine life itself. It caused them to flow into the three states of final confinement [GAP-1: …] which it had established during the formation of the mind's structures [GAP-2: …] they [GAP-3: …] yet something remained behind in the outermost surface of the natural mind from these three containing forms of evil, so that one can find their trace and representative image displayed throughout the whole created order of the mind.

**¶4:** The element that remains from falsity is the bitterness and corrosive quality of that pervading body of corrupted knowledge — the great encircling sea of adulterated learning — which surrounds all the interior structures of the mind.

**¶5:** And the remnant that remains from spiritual darkness is that state of dense self-obscurity and prideful elevation that persists at the very boundary where divine wisdom first rises. For when divine wisdom shines over the mind, no illumination can be perceived there, because the falsity from evil that issues forth from that state of pride casts its shadow continually above it.

**¶6:** And the remnant that remains from evil love, within the natural mind, consists of all those states of self-exaltation and isolated conditions of the will from which the exhalations of selfish desire ascend and become manifest. For these are the remnant of the great containing form of infernal love, the vestige that was conjoined with the self-love that rises from the natural mind; together with the states of pride and self-elevation [GAP-4: …] states where no good works proceed from the perceptions [GAP-5: …] greater than that state, from the faculty and [GAP-6: … / …] the perceptions shall not bring forth good works in that state.

**¶7:** Why were these evils not expelled from the interior mind directly into the places of confinement prepared for them? Why were they first poured into the natural mind, and only afterward swept from the natural mind and cast down into their final states of containment?

**¶8:** When Divine Providence expelled these containing forms from the interior mind upon the natural mind, it poured them down for this reason: so that the falsity, the spiritual darkness, and the evil love already dwelling within the natural planes of the mind would be drawn out and ascend toward their corresponding evils that had descended from above, and thus the natural mind would be thoroughly purified and cleansed. For this purpose it brought these containing forms down into the natural mind — of falsity, of darkness, and of evil love — so that the falsity, darkness, and evil love already rooted within the natural planes would be drawn upward by affinity toward what had descended from the interior.

**¶9:** First of all, Divine Providence expelled the falsity — the waste, the spiritual poison of the ruling evils that inhabit the interior mind. It cleansed the rational faculties of [GAP-7: falsity …] and poured down the darkened falsities. [GAP-8: And just as] these falsities descended from the interior mind into the natural mind, so also the falsities dwelling below in the natural planes were drawn upward from beneath toward the falsities that had come from above into the natural mind. The falsities [GAP-9: were thus] purified of the destructive spiritual poison that existed within them. Then Divine Providence swept them outward and formed them into a great containing boundary — a surrounding wall of general knowledge encircling the whole mind — upon which the doctrinal systems of understanding navigate.

**¶10:** After the falsity, Divine Providence expelled the spiritual darkness. It purified the rational faculties and dried from them the obscurity by which they were weighed down. It brought this darkness down into the natural mind. Just as it had purified the rational faculties, so also it purified the natural planes. The spiritual darkness dwelling within the natural mind was drawn upward toward the darkness that had been expelled from above. Divine Providence swept both out together and confined them in that [GAP-10: …] state of spiritual darkness [GAP-11: … / …] the falsity.

**¶11:** And it expelled the evil love from the interior mind into the natural, [GAP-12: … and at] that time again the evil love that was confined [GAP-13: within] the natural mind below was drawn upward toward its own kind. Evil love was joined to evil love. Afterward, Divine Providence swept the whole of it out and cast it into the outermost infernal state, which [GAP-14: it had formed for] them beyond the boundaries of the mind's entire order.

**¶12:** In the same way that Divine Providence purified the rational faculties above as a pathway for the bearers of wisdom to journey through [GAP-15: … / …] so also it purified the natural planes below and swept from them the evil love, the spiritual darkness, and the falsity [GAP-16: …]. It purified them for the ascent of the three genuine powers of spiritual life — those of spiritual influx, of truth, and of love in their uncorrupted forms — which ascend before the Guardian of the threshold and traverse the planes of the natural mind from lowest to highest.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: When the Father of Life discharged these three vessels from above, they of water and of darkness and of fire, did he perhaps discharge them to their pits at the edge of the firmament? Or did he discharge them first to this earth, and then he swept them from the earth and threw them to their places?

when the Father of Life was about to discharge these three vessels he poured the three upon this earth, one by one at its (appointed) hour and season. He discharged them and cast them down to the earth.

Then he bailed and scooped them from this earth in these three garments, they of wind and of water and of fire, which swathed his body. He poured and made them flow into the three pits [prepared for them]hich he had [es]tablished during the construc[tio]n of the worlds [Yet when] they [were swept away] something remained behind on the face of the earth from these three vessels, so that you can find their mark and type displayed in the universe.
The element that is left in water is the pungency and the salinity of this salty inner sea that surrounds the worlds.

And the remnant that is left from the darkness is this black mountain that exists in the surroundings of the sunrise. For when the sun would shine over the world no sunlight is visible there, because the darkness that gushes from it manifests above it.

And the remnant that remains behind from the fire, upon the earth, are all the mountains and islands from where fumes of fire gush up and are visible. For these things are the remnant of the great vessel, the vestige that was conjoined with this fire that comes up from the earth; together with the mountains and hills [and all the] places where no fruit sprouts on the trees [for the fire is] greater than that place from the limb and [ ... / ... ] the trees shall not bear fruit in that place.

why they were not discharged from above into the ditches prepared for them (straightaway); but were firstly poured upon the earth, and afterwards were swept from the earth and cast down into their pits?

When the Father of Life discharged these vessels from above upon the earth, he poured them out for this reason: so that also the water and the darkness and the fire that exist in these three earths would be drawn and ascend towards they that had come down from above, and the earths would be purified and cleansed. Due to this he poured these vessels down to the earth, of water and of darkness and of fire, so that also the water and darkness and fire that exist in the earths would be drawn up towards they that had descended from above.

Now, first of all, he discharged the water, the waste, the poison of the rulers who are above. He cleansed the firmaments of the [that burdened them] he poured down the dark waters. [Just as the] waters fell from heaven to earth, so also the waters below in the earths were drawn and came up from below towards the waters that had come from above to the earths. The waters [were] purified of the dark poison that exists in them. Then he swept them outside and made them a great vessel and a wall of sea that surrounds the universe, and on which the ships sail.

After the water, he discharged the darkness. He purified the firmaments and dried from them the darkness with which they are weighed down. He discharged it down to the earth. Just as he had purified the firmaments, so also he purified the earths. The darkness that is in the earths was drawn up towards the darkness that had been discharged from above. He swept them both out and shut them in that [pit] of darkness [ ... / ... ] the water.

And he discharged the fire from heaven to earth, [and] that time again the fire that was shut [in] the earth below was drawn and came up towards its kind. Fire was added to fire. Afterwards, he swept it out and cast it into the outer underworld, which [he had constructed for] them outside the universe.

In the same way that he purified the firmaments above as a place for the light-givers to journey [ ... / ... ] so also he purified the earths below and swept from them the fire and the darkness and the water [that was in them] He has purified them for the ascent of these three powers, they of the wind and the water and the fire, which ascend before the Porter and traverse the earths.

fills.explanation: Directly echoes ¶7's phrase "the ditches prepared for them," which describes the same pits using identical language, and the spiritual reading's "states of final confinement" confirms these are pre-established receptacles.
The spiritual reading's "yet" signals an adversative transition — the vessels were removed but something remained — requiring a concessive conjunction before "they" as subject of GAP-3's verb.

The text's core vocabulary for removing the vessels is "swept" (bail, scoop, sweep — used in ¶3, ¶7, ¶8, ¶9, ¶10, ¶11), and "they" (the three vessels) need a passive verb before "something remained behind."
The passage lists the remnants of fire as mountains, islands, and then further barren places; "and all the" is the standard Kephalaia connector extending a catalogue of cosmological locations.

The spiritual reading indicates that evil love (fire) overwhelms the faculty (limb) at that state, preventing good works (fruit); "for the fire is greater than that place" explains why no fruit sprouts — the fire's intensity overpowers the place's capacity for growth.

Parallels the identical construction in ¶10 where the firmaments are cleansed of "the darkness with which they are weighed down"; the spiritual reading confirms the firmaments/rational faculties were laden with falsity/water that needed removal.

Confirming the editor's choice: the "Just as... so also" construction directly parallels the identical formula in ¶10 ("Just as he had purified the firmaments, so also he purified the earths"), establishing the descent-ascent correspondence pattern.

Confirming the editor's choice: the simple passive "were purified" matches the impersonal expository register of the Kephalaia and the parallel constructions throughout the chapter describing purification of elements.

The text consistently uses "pits" (¶1, ¶7) for the places of confinement where the three vessels are cast; "shut them in that pit of darkness" parallels the phrasing throughout the chapter and matches the spiritual reading's "state of confinement."

The spiritual reading explicitly marks "and at" as the transition, and the simple conjunction "and" connects the discharge of fire from heaven to the consequent drawing-up of fire from below, matching the narrative flow of ¶9 and ¶10.

Confirming the editor's choice: "the fire that was shut in the earth below" uses the standard Kephalaia locative for elements confined within the earths, directly paralleling ¶8's "the fire that exist in the earths."

Confirming the editor's choice: "constructed" belongs to the same semantic field as "established during the construction of the worlds" (¶3) and "prepared" (¶7), describing the Father of Life's prior building of containment structures.

Directly echoes ¶8's repeated formula "the water and darkness and fire that exist in the earths" — the three elements swept from the earths are those "that was in them," completing the purification summary.
